resources.string: Finds interface elements selected by the user, captures the screen only when visual selection is requested, and performs explicitly configured workflow actions.
Capture the target app, then drag over the area to recognize. At runtime, a click occurs only for a unique match.
Lower values tolerate more visual change but increase false-match risk. Default: 92.0%.
A second match within this margin prevents the click. Lower values accept closer alternatives. Default: 2.5%.
More sampled sizes handle common display or zoom changes but take more matching time. Intermediate sizes and rotation are not included.
Enter a value from 0.0 to 100.0 with at most one decimal place.

When you request screenshot selection, the app captures the target screen for visual selection, coordinate gestures, or an image-click template. Full screenshots stay only in memory until you finish or cancel, replace or clear them, stop the accessibility service, or end the app process. They are never saved or uploaded.

When enabled, AI Index Finger reads visible screen text, descriptions, view identifiers, and app names so you can inspect elements and run workflows you create.

While running a workflow, the app can click, swipe, enter text, use system navigation, and temporarily replace clipboard content for pasting. It restores the original clipboard content if it has not changed again.
Observed interface data and run history stay on this device. The app has no network permission and does not send this data elsewhere. You can disable the service at any time in Android settings.
